recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中一個巨噬細胞內塞滿無色、具稜角（長方形或六角形）的折光性結晶，偏光顯微鏡下呈多彩強雙折射，為胱胺酸（cystine）結晶沉積，提示胱胺酸症（cystinosis）。
features: Macrophage with cytoplasm packed by numerous colorless, refractile, angular crystals (rectangular to polygonal/hexagonal) (B)
Crystals displace the nucleus to the periphery and give the cell a glassy, stuffed appearance
Polarized light (A): strong multicolored birefringence of the intracellular crystals, standing out against a dark background
Surrounding marrow shows normal-appearing maturing granulocytic and erythroid elements
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a histiocyte distended by innumerable colorless, refractile, angular rectangular to polygonal crystals that push the nucleus aside; the background hematopoiesis appears otherwise unremarkable in this field. Under polarized light the intracellular crystals display intense, multicolored birefringence. Findings are consistent with cystine crystal deposition in marrow macrophages, suggestive of cystinosis; confirmation by leukocyte cystine measurement and CTNS genetic testing is recommended.

ddx.vs: Immunoglobulin crystals are eosinophilic/pale blue needle or rhomboid shapes that are usually weakly or non-birefringent and are light-chain restricted by IHC, often with a plasma cell neoplasm.
Oxalate crystals are birefringent rosettes or sheaves in marrow causing fibrosis and granulomatous reaction, often extracellular and in primary hyperoxaluria with renal failure.
Gaucher cells have fibrillar wrinkled tissue-paper cytoplasm without discrete refractile crystals or birefringence.
Charcot-Leyden crystals are slender bipyramidal needles derived from eosinophils rather than clustered polygonal crystals within macrophages.

captions: Polarized light: brightly birefringent crystals within a macrophage
